definition.simple: How much a test result changes when you nudge a setting, such as an average length from 20 to 18 or 22.
definition.balanced: If neighbouring settings give similar results, the result is less fragile. A single sharp peak surrounded by losses is a warning sign of [[overfitting]]. Low sensitivity does not prove a rule has an edge; it only shows the result does not hinge on one exact number.

example: Lengths 16 to 24 give −4R, −1R, +12R, −2R, −5R: the +12R at length 20 stands alone and is fragile.
